AI.tldr: This paper identifies complex nitrogen-bearing molecules (CH₃CN, C₂H₅CN, C₂H₃CN, NH₂CN, NH₂CHO, and vibrationally excited HC₃N) toward the high-mass protostar S255IR NIRS3 using ALMA band 4. LTE modeling yields excitation temperatures of 175–220 K, indicating warm inner regions. Abundance correlations reveal strong links among cyanide-family molecules (r > 0.7), and comparisons with three-phase warm-up chemical models show good agreement (within factors of ~0.67–1.28). Formation pathways via gas-grain chemistry are discussed.
AI.motivation: To probe the physical and chemical evolution of star-forming regions by studying complex nitrogen-bearing molecules, which are key tracers of warm, chemically active environments in high-mass protostellar sources.
AI.method: ALMA band 4 observations of S255IR NIRS3; identification of rotational emission lines; LTE spectral modeling to derive column densities and excitation temperatures; fractional abundance estimation relative to H₂, CH₃OH, and CH₃CN; Pearson correlation analysis; comparison with three-phase warm-up chemical models.
AI.result: Detection of multiple N-bearing molecules including CH₃CN, C₂H₅CN, C₂H₃CN, NH₂CN, NH₂CHO, and HC₃N (ν₇=2). Excitation temperatures of 175–220 K. Strong positive abundance correlation (r > 0.7) among CH₃CN, C₂H₃CN, and C₂H₅CN. Model-predicted abundances agree with observations within factors of 0.67–1.28.
AI.conclusion: The identified N-bearing molecules originate from warm inner regions (≥100 K) of S255IR NIRS3. The strong abundance correlations suggest chemical links within the cyanide family. The observed abundances are well reproduced by gas-grain chemical models, supporting the proposed formation pathways in high-mass star-forming regions.

title: For modified gravity, it's the LITTLE THINGS that matter
summary: Dwarf galaxies have long been recognised as important testing grounds for models of dark matter. For instance, it is here where the cusp-core problem is most apparent. In this work we select two dwarf galaxy samples: LITTLE THINGS and dwarf galaxies in SPARC. We use these to examine whether there are preferences for MOND or dark matter halos in these objects. Notably, our analysis employs the latest developments in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling methodology and robust model comparison via ELPD differences. Our findings suggest a $>4σ$ preference for cored halo models over MOND. However, this relies on significant preferences from 7 out of 19 SPARC galaxies and 11 of 18 from LITTLE THINGS (few of which are overwhelming). It is notable that only a single galaxy prefers MOND over a cored halo. Thus, this evidence is suggestive, but does not conclusively decide against MOND. We also test for evidence of a MOND external field effect, and find weak evidence against its presence. Despite these statistical preferences, most SPARC galaxies remain compatible with a universal MOND scale. In LITTLE THINGS, a free MOND model is preferred to a universal value at $\sim 8σ$, but this is of doubtful physical significance. For MOG, the story is different, here we find $\gtrsim 8σ$ preferences for all halos (or MOND) against universal MOG models with significant exclusions in individual galaxies across both samples. Thus, a proposed universal rotation curve model derived from MOG is quite strongly disfavoured.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes two dwarf galaxy samples (LITTLE THINGS and SPARC) using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and ELPD model comparison, finding a >4σ preference for cored dark matter halos over MOND, though mostly driven by a subset of galaxies; MOND's universal scale is still compatible with most SPARC galaxies, while universal MOG models are very strongly disfavored (>8σ) across both samples.
AI.motivation: Dwarf galaxies are key testing grounds for dark matter models, particularly the cusp-core problem, and the authors aim to statistically compare the viability of MOND, dark matter halos, and MOG using rigorous Bayesian model comparison.
AI.method: The study uses two dwarf galaxy samples (LITTLE THINGS and SPARC) and applies Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling for inference, with model comparison via ELPD (Expected Log Predictive Density) differences.
AI.result: A >4σ preference for cored halo models over MOND is found, but this is driven by preferences in 7/19 SPARC and 11/18 LITTLE THINGS galaxies; only one galaxy prefers MOND over a cored halo. Weak evidence against the MOND external field effect is found. Universal MOG models are disfavored at >8σ.
AI.conclusion: The evidence is suggestive against MOND but not conclusive; most SPARC galaxies remain compatible with a universal MOND scale. A universal MOG rotation curve model is strongly disfavored.

title: The first near-infrared high-resolution échelle spectroscopy of the outflow in NGC 4151. A study of the clouds covering the Eye of Sauron
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication on Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We present the first high-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy of the nucleus of the nearby, well-known Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151 (the "Eye of Sauron"). Past studies of this source have revealed that it exhibits a variable absorption feature associated with the He I $λ$10,830 AA emission line, potentially indicative of obscuration events affecting the central engine. Here, we take advantage of the IRTF/iSHELL and TNG/GIANO-B spectrographs to observe this feature with unprecedented spectral resolution ($λ/Δλ> 50,000$), being able to study in detail the structure of the absorption trough and its variations over a time span of $\sim$700 days. In order to infer a connection between the He I absorption variability and that of the X-ray ionising continuum, we also analyse the publicly available data collected by the Swift-XRT instrument over the same period of time, unveiling a potential driving mechanism in the changes of the outflow ionisation state due to the X-ray flux variations. We also derive outflow physical parameters - $\dot{M}_{\rm out} \lesssim 10^{-2}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, $r_{\rm out} \sim 3$ pc, $v_{\rm max} \sim 1000$ km s$^{-1}$ - that are in line with those of comparable ionised winds found in similar targets, where the outflow is not powerful enough to trigger a significant AGN feedback ($\dot{E}_{\rm kin}/L_{\rm bol} \sim 0.001$%). Such findings point at a scenario in which a dusty and clumpy outflow that obscures NGC 4151 up to galactic scales responds to changes in the ionising X-ray flux, similarly to what happens in quasars with broad absorption lines and Seyferts with multiphase outflows such as NGC 5548.

AI.tldr: High-resolution near-IR spectroscopy of NGC 4151 reveals variable He I absorption at 10,830 Å linked to X-ray-driven changes in the ionized outflow, with modest kinetic power (~0.001% L_bol) insufficient for significant AGN feedback.
AI.motivation: To study variable He I absorption features in NGC 4151's nucleus at high spectral resolution, and link their variability to X-ray ionizing continuum changes to understand obscuration events and outflow driving mechanisms.
AI.method: High-resolution near-IR spectroscopy (IRTF/iSHELL & TNG/GIANO-B, R>50,000) over ~700 days, combined with Swift-XRT X-ray monitoring, to analyze He I λ10,830 Å absorption variability and its correlation with the ionizing continuum.
AI.result: Outflow parameters: Ṁ_out ≲ 10⁻² M⊙ yr⁻¹, r_out ~ 3 pc, v_max ~ 1000 km s⁻¹, kinetic power ~0.001% L_bol. He I absorption variability is driven by changes in the X-ray flux modulating the outflow ionization state.
AI.conclusion: NGC 4151 hosts a dusty, clumpy outflow responding to X-ray ionizing flux variations, similar to quasars with BALs and Seyferts like NGC 5548, but with insufficient power for significant AGN feedback.

title: First Light and Reionization Epoch Simulations (FLARES) XXII: UV-dust spatial offsets at the Epoch of Reionisation
summary: Recent observations have revealed intriguing offsets between the UV and FIR emission in high redshift galaxies. In this study, we use the First Light And Reionisation Epoch Simulations (\textsc{Flares}) to compute the spatial offset of ultraviolet (UV) and far-infrared (FIR) centres for a statistical sample (6890) of massive (M$_{\star}\, \gtrsim10^{9} \,{\rm M_{\odot}}$) high redshift galaxies ($z \in [5,10]$). The galaxies are post-processed with the \textsc{skirt} radiative transfer code, to obtain the full spectral energy distribution and surface brightness profile. We simulate \textit{James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)} Near Infrared Camera (NIRCam; rest-frame 1500 Å, $ \approx 0.031 ''$ resolution) and ALMA rest-frame 158 \um\ ($\approx$ $0.3''$ angular resolution) observations of the galaxies and then calculate the distance between the UV-FIR centres to analyse which physical processes drive the observed UV - FIR spatial offset. We find that $\sim16.23\%$ of galaxies exhibit spatial offsets of $\geq 2.5$ kpc between their UV and FIR emission peaks. We establish that the spatial offsets do not correlate with stellar mass, UV/FIR luminosity, and size. Offsets also do not correlate with AGN feedback or with large-scale environment or merger history. Galaxies with significant offsets preferentially have bluer UV slopes ($-2.5<β<-1.5$), consistent with recent star formation and dust-attenuated cores displacing the observed UV centroid. They show an accelerated star formation history, forming half their $z=5$ stellar mass $\sim$0.1 Gyr earlier than galaxies without offsets. These galaxies are enriched earlier than galaxies without an offset and show enhanced stellar metallicities, indicating a transition to an outward growth at higher redshifts ($z \geq 6$).

AI.tldr: Using FLARES simulations and radiative transfer post-processing, the study finds that ~16% of massive high-z galaxies (z=5-10) show UV-FIR spatial offsets ≥2.5 kpc. Offsets are uncorrelated with stellar mass, luminosity, size, AGN feedback, environment, or mergers, but are linked to bluer UV slopes, accelerated star formation histories, earlier enrichment, and outward growth at z≥6.
AI.motivation: Recent observations have revealed intriguing offsets between UV and FIR emission in high-redshift galaxies, motivating a systematic investigation of the physical origins and statistical properties of these spatial offsets.
AI.method: The authors use FLARES simulations with SKIRT radiative transfer to model SEDs and surface brightness profiles of 6890 massive galaxies at z=5-10. They simulate JWST NIRCam (1500 Å, 0.031") and ALMA (158 μm, 0.3") observations and measure UV-FIR centroid distances.
AI.result: ~16.23% of galaxies show offsets ≥2.5 kpc. Offsets do not correlate with stellar mass, UV/FIR luminosity, size, AGN feedback, environment, or mergers. Offset galaxies have bluer UV slopes, accelerated star formation histories (forming half their mass ~0.1 Gyr earlier), earlier enrichment, and enhanced stellar metallicities, indicating outward growth at z≥6.
AI.conclusion: UV-FIR spatial offsets in high-z galaxies are driven by recent star formation and dust-attenuated cores displacing the UV centroid, with offset galaxies exhibiting earlier formation, faster enrichment, and outward growth at higher redshifts.
